sections.h2: Which ways of selling are open to a Cibolo homeowner?
sections.html:
Cibolo homeowners generally choose between an agent's listing, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash purchase that leaves the house untouched. Repair needs and your calendar decide.

  • Agent: wide exposure, with showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal to wait through.
  • Do-it-yourself: you handle pricing, negotiation and contract details.
  • Cash purchase: removes repair requests and the loan step, which helps with inherited houses, rentals and deadlines.

A few Cibolo details shape any route: the city's place east of San Antonio, a county line that runs nearby, and a permit office that runs through one online portal.

sections.h2: Where is Cibolo and how did the city grow?
sections.html:
Cibolo lies in the extreme western corner of Guadalupe County, along FM 78 and FM 1103, with Interstate 10 to the south and Interstate 35 to the north, about 13 miles east of the San Antonio metropolitan area, according to the city's own history page. The city places itself in the Metrocom, the northeast corner of Bexar County and southwest corner of Guadalupe County, with Schertz, Universal City, Selma, Live Oak, Garden Ridge, Converse and Kirby as neighbors. Randolph Air Force Base, a pilot training facility, is nearby.

The name is an Indian word for buffalo, and the town took the name of the creek. The city says its story begins in 1876, when the Southern Pacific Railroad came through and linked the farms to Houston and San Antonio. Cotton was the main cash crop for decades, along with corn, wheat, oats and milo maize. Cibolo voted to become an independent township on October 9, 1965.

The city's census figures show the scale of the change: 440 people in 1970, 1,757 in 1990, 3,035 in 2000, 19,580 in 2010 after a challenge to the count, and an estimated 37,061 as of 2023.

sections.h2: Does Cibolo property sit in Bexar County or Guadalupe County?
sections.html:
The city's own text puts Cibolo in Guadalupe County and describes the surrounding Metrocom as reaching into northeast Bexar County, so confirm the tax roll for your parcel on your statement before pricing.

Every Texas district prices property on January 1 and mails notices in spring. According to the Comptroller, bills are mailed near October 1, and what is still unpaid on February 1 draws a six percent penalty and one percent interest. The penalty keeps growing a point a month until it reaches 12 percent in July.

A homestead owner receives a $140,000 school district exemption, and that home's appraised value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year. A buyer files a new application after closing. For a balance and current adopted rates, ask the county tax office rather than an online estimator.

sections.h2: Who issues permits in Cibolo, and why does it come up at closing?
sections.html:
The Cibolo Building and Permitting Department handles permits and inspections, and it asks everyone to apply through the MGO Connect portal. The department is at 201 West Loop 539, and its main office number is (210) 658-4175.

Your most useful step is to find any permit tied to your address and see whether it was closed. The city's portal lets you look up a permit, and the office email is permitting@cibolotx.gov. A deck, a pool, a new water heater, a patio cover or an addition without a final inspection is the kind of item that holds up a title company or a buyer's inspector.

sections.h2: What building codes and inspection rules apply to repairs in Cibolo?
sections.html:
Cibolo adopted the 2021 editions of the International Building, Residential, Energy Conservation, Plumbing, Fuel Gas, Mechanical, Swimming Pool and Spa, and Fire Codes, together with the 2023 National Electrical Code, under Ordinance 1475. Local amendments are listed on the city's Codes and Fees pages.

The city states a few working rules for permit holders:

  • Contractors must register before they submit a permit application.
  • An account in the portal is required before any application.
  • Permits, inspections and permit lookups all run through the same portal.

Before starting repairs, ask the office whether the work needs a permit. Selling as-is instead? Put any unfinished work in writing for the buyer.

The city's FAQ adds practical detail for homeowners. A shed needs a permit if it sits on a permanent foundation, cannot be moved once installed, or exceeds 100 square feet. Water heaters, roof work, replacement HVAC, electrical, plumbing, irrigation and water softener permits can be issued at submittal without plan review. Residential plan reviews may take up to 10 business days, and the city has no process to expedite them. Garage sales need no permit, though the signs do, and signs must come down within 48 hours.

sections.h2: What should a Cibolo seller know about utilities and annexed land?
sections.html:
City Utility Services at Cibolo City Hall, 200 South Main Street, handles water and wastewater accounts, and the FAQ says the city does not currently waive deposits or administration fees. Tell your buyer which utility account to open, and close your own account as part of the move.

If your land was recently annexed, the city's FAQ cites Texas Local Government Code Chapter 43 and lists what changes: voting rights and representation, public street maintenance, land use and density rules through zoning, and code enforcement. It also says an agricultural exemption can continue while the property keeps qualifying, and that the city does not expect address changes. Buyers of acreage on the edge of town should ask the planning staff how the city's zoning treats the parcel.

sections.h2: What if my Cibolo house is in probate, has a tenant or is near foreclosure?
sections.html:
Texas puts different clocks on each.

  • Probate: four years from death to probate a will, with court discretion afterward. Heirs may file an affidavit of heirship with the clerk, but a title company is free to refuse it.
  • Tenant: written notice to vacate of at least 3 days, then a justice court case, and a writ of possession no sooner than 6 days after judgment.
  • Foreclosure: a courthouse auction on a first Tuesday; if the lender later sues for a deficiency, it must do so within two years of the sale.

With two or more of these in play, a cash buyer can often work around them, but the title company still needs documents showing who has authority to sign.

faqs.a: The city's own history page places Cibolo in the extreme western corner of Guadalupe County, and says the surrounding Metrocom area covers northeast Bexar County. Check your tax statement to see which appraisal district holds your parcel.

faqs.q: How do I check for an open permit on my Cibolo house?
faqs.a: Use the MGO Connect portal, which has a permit lookup, or contact permitting@cibolotx.gov or (210) 658-4175. Closing any open permit before you list helps the sale move.

faqs.q: Which building codes does Cibolo enforce?
faqs.a: Cibolo enforces the 2021 International codes and the 2023 National Electrical Code under Ordinance 1475. The Codes and Fees section of the city site lists the local amendments.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They are delinquent on February 1 if unpaid by the end of January, per the Texas Comptroller, and a penalty plus interest begin to accrue.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell a Cibolo house without a full probate case?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A muniment of title or small estate affidavit can work when the estate qualifies and a court approves it. A probate attorney can say which route fits your family.
